newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-Italian debt vol steady,l-term trend down.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Italian debt vol steady,l-term trend down.

text.p: Implied volatility of BTP and Eurolira options was steady to slightly lower on Monday after the Bank of Italy cut interest rates on Friday.
But traders say the long-term volatility trend for Italian interest rate options is downwards.

"The Italian money curve has been so inverted for so long, and the cost of carry was so high, that the rate cut was more a relief than anything else," said one options dealer from a U.S. bank in Paris.

The Bank of Italy cut the official discount rate by 50 basis points to 6.25 percent, its lowest level for almost 22 years, and its fixed term advances (Lombard rate) by 50 basis points to 7.75 percent.

Implied volatility of September Eurolira was quoted at 12.14 percent bid at 1240 GMT, against 12.25 percent on Friday. December Eurolira volatility also dipped slightly, to 14.75 percent bid from 15.33 percent.
September Eurolira futures were seven basis points higher on the day at 93.51, while December Eurolire gained three basis points to 93.89.
In BTP options, September was unchanged at 7.30-7.60 percent, the U.S. bank trader said. September BTP futures gained 17 basis points to 134.25.
Options trading was thin, dealers said.
"When you see the price that the BTP has been at, it's not surprising," said one options trader from a European bank in London.
BTP futures reached an all-time high of 134.84 on Thursday, and options traders did not expect major price fluctuation this week, keeping the lid on volatility levels.
"There has been a little volatility selling," the European bank trader added.
Longer-term, implied volatility of Italian options will fall to move into line with German interest rate options ahead of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), the U.S. bank trader said.
"As the market gets news that EMU is going to happen, volatility in Italy will converge with Germany."
